title: Working at Redwood: roles, career ladders, benefits, hiring & onboarding, and internal tools
author: Maya Singh
body:
Overview

This document is the canonical company handbook entry for engineers, product managers, and cross-functional partners joining or working at Redwood Inference. It covers: how we work, role families and career ladders, benefits & perks, a high-level hiring and onboarding overview, and the core internal tools and provisioning steps every new employee needs. Use this page as a starting point and follow links to team-specific guides for role-specific expectations and ramp plans.

1) How we work (culture & operating principles)

- Developer-first mindset: we prioritize tooling, reproducibility, and measurable performance for production LLM inference.
- Outcomes over activities: managers and ICs are evaluated on delivering customer-facing outcomes, product impact, and operational reliability.
- Blameless postmortems and continuous improvement: incidents, experiments, and rollouts follow a clear review loop and actionable ownership.
- Open collaboration: documentation-first approach (Confluence + PRs), async-first communication, regular demos and cross-team syncs.

2) Roles and career ladders (global overview)

This section summarizes our primary role families and typical progression. Detailed leveled expectations and rubrics live in the team-level career ladders linked at the bottom.

Engineering individual contributor ladder (common titles):
| Level | Typical title | Focus / expectations |
|---|---|---|
| IC1 | Software Engineer I | Deliver well-scoped features with mentorship, reliable unit-level ownership.
| IC2 | Software Engineer II | Feature ownership across services, contributes to design, independently ships.
| IC3 | Senior Software Engineer | Leads design for cross-service features, mentors peers, improves operational posture.
| IC4 | Staff Engineer | Technical leader across teams, sets architecture and roadmap direction, influences company-wide practices.
| IC5 | Principal / Distinguished | Strategic technical vision, long-term platform investments, trusted advisor to execs.

Engineering manager ladder (common titles):
- Manager -> Senior Manager -> Director of Engineering -> Senior Director -> VP of Engineering
- People managers are measured on team outcomes, hiring & development, cross-functional delivery, and operational health.

Product & Design ladder summary:
- Product Manager I/II/Senior/Product Lead/Group PM -> Director/VP
- Product Designers follow a parallel IC ladder (Designer, Senior, Lead, Principal).

Performance & promotion notes:
- Promotions require documented evidence against role rubric: scope, impact, technical or product leadership, and collaboration.
- Promotion cycle: managers nominate, peer reviews collected, final decision aligned with calibration committee. Check team career ladder doc for level-specific artifacts and examples.

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

Core benefits (US / global variants explained by People Ops):
- Health: medical, dental, and vision coverage with company contribution tiers.
- Financial: competitive salary, equity grants, and 401(k) with partial employer match (region-dependent).
- Parental leave: primary and secondary caregiver leave, flexible return-to-work options.
- Time off: flexible PTO policy plus company-observed holidays.
- Stipends: home office allowance on hire and periodic remote-work stipend.
- Learning & development: annual education stipend ($1,500 USD standard), conference budget, and internal learning cohorts.
- Wellness: Employee Assistance Program (EAP), mental health coverage, and monthly wellness stipend.

Perks and recognition:
- Referral bonuses for successful hires.
- Monthly knowledge-sharing lunches and regular team offsites.
- Early access to company demos and product credits for experimentation.

How to access benefits:
1. Visit the benefits portal (link in People Ops Confluence).
2. Complete required elections within 30 days of hire.
3. Contact benefits@redwood.com for exceptions or region-specific questions.

4) Hiring overview (high-level process)

Our hiring process balances candidate experience with rigor. Below is the standard loop for engineering and product roles; variations exist for internships, early-career, and executive hires.

Standard hiring loop (engineering):
1. Recruiter screen: role fit, timeline, compensation expectations.
2. Technical phone screen: 45–60 minutes, coding problem and systems discussion.
3. Onsite / loop (4–5 interviews, 2–3 hours remote): coding, system design, product sense (if applicable), and collaboration/culture fit.
4. Hiring manager debrief & comp/doc package creation.
5. Reference checks (as required) and offer.
6. Background check and pre-hire compliance (region dependent).

Interview best practices and scoring:
- Interviewers use standardized rubrics (technical, problem solving, communication, role-specific competencies).
- Interview debriefs must be submitted within 48 hours. Recruiters collect feedback and run calibration when necessary.

Diversity & inclusion measures:
- Diverse interview panels encouraged; removal of non-essential requirements on job descriptions; active sourcing and partnerships.

5) Onboarding overview (first 90 days)

New hire ramp plan (recommended 90-day outline):
- Day 0–7: paperwork completed, access provisioned, intro to team rituals, first-week orientation session.
- Weeks 2–4: small starter project assigned, buddy assigned, regular 1:1s scheduled with manager.
- Months 1–3: progressively larger ownership, cross-team introductions, first performance checkpoint at 30 days and 90-day onboarding review.

New hire checklist (minimum):
1. Accept offer and complete benefits elections.
2. Complete I-9 / local compliance forms where required.
3. Setup Okta SSO and company email.
4. Join core Slack channels: #company-all, #eng, #people-ops, #<team-name>.
5. Gain GitHub access and join team repos.
6. Complete dev environment setup using the team README + dev bootstrap script.
7. Schedule 1:1 with manager and assigned buddy.

Manager responsibilities in onboarding:
- Provide clear first-week goals and the starter project.
- Assign a buddy and schedule cross-functional intros.
- Ensure access and tools are provisioned within 48 hours.
- Run the 30/60/90 check-ins and give timely feedback.

6) Internal tools & provisioning (quick reference)

Primary tooling we use (examples and pointers):
- Identity & SSO: Okta (primary SSO provider) — you will receive an Okta invite on your hire date.
- Password manager: 1Password (company vault) — join via Okta, follow the onboarding guide to claim an account.
- Source control: GitHub Enterprise — request team repo access via the GitHub self-service tool (link in Confluence).
- Issue tracking: Linear (or team-specified alternatives) — your team lead will invite you to team boards.
- Communication: Slack — core channels include #company-all, #eng, #product, #sre, and team channels.
- Docs & knowledge base: Confluence (this handbook) and shared team spaces.
- CI/CD: Buildkite and internal deploy pipelines — request pipeline permissions through eng-infra oncall.
- Pager & oncall: PagerDuty — engineers oncall will be added to relevant schedules; see eng-sre runbooks for escalation paths.

Provisioning flow (typical timeline):
- Day 0: People Ops triggers Okta invite and 1Password invite.
- Day 0–1: GitHub access requested and provisioned, Slack invited.
- Day 1–3: AWS/GCP console and internal monitoring dashboards access; request credentials via the cloud-accounts-and-networking playbook.

Common support contacts:
- Access & provisioning issues: access-requests@redwood.com (People Ops)
- IT & hardware: it-ops@redwood.com
- Payroll & benefits: payroll@redwood.com
- New-hire logistics and questions: onboarding@redwood.com

7) Manager & peer expectations (day-to-day)

- Managers: set clear goals (OKRs/KRs), remove blockers, run career conversations quarterly, and own compensation calibration input.
- Peers: practice code review standards, contribute to runbooks, and help maintain team documentation.
- All employees: keep Confluence pages up to date for systems you own; add clear runbooks for production services.

8) HR policies summary and where to find them

- Time off & leave policy: see People Ops > time-off and leave page.
- Performance reviews: cycle and rubric in People Ops performance & calibration page.
- Code of conduct & anti-harassment: available in company policies.

9) Frequently asked questions (short)

Q: Who should I contact if I don’t have access to a repo?
A: File a ticket to access-requests@redwood.com and cc your manager.

Q: How do I request equipment?
A: Email it-ops@redwood.com with role, laptop preference, and justification. The home office stipend can be used for peripherals.

Q: Where are detailed career ladder rubrics?
A: See team-level career ladder pages linked from the People Ops career hub.

10) Ownership and related pages

- Document owner: People Ops (contact: onboarding@redwood.com).
- Maintenance cadence: review annually or whenever benefits / policy changes occur.
- Related pages: team-specific onboarding guides, engineering career ladders (eng-developer-experience), and benefits portal.

Links and templates (examples to copy):
- New hire 30/60/90 template: /confluence/company-handbook/new-hire-30-60-90-template
- Manager onboarding checklist: /confluence/company-handbook/manager-onboarding-checklist
- Team career ladder index: /confluence/people-ops/career-ladders

If you have questions or suggested updates to this handbook entry, open a PR on this Confluence page or email onboarding@redwood.com.
